Let me start by understanding the situation better. We live in a dorm room with two beds and desks, pretty standard. My boyfriend and I were in our room, just watching Netflix on my bed. It's a pretty normal evening, nothing out of the ordinary. But then my roommate and her friend started doing this thing that's really annoying. Every time they leave the room, they leave the door wide open. They laugh and say "this is what you get" as if it's some kind of joke for showing minimal PDA with my boyfriend in my room. I mean, we're just watching Netflix, nothing more. But the fact that they leave the door open is super annoying and makes me uncomfortable. People in the dorm walk by, and I don't want them to see me in my bed. It's a matter of privacy, right? Plus, they're doing this intentionally to make me feel that way. Tonight, they took it a step further. They left the room giggling and said "good luck" as they left the door open. They do this going in and out of the room like five times an hour. Each time, I get up and close the door. I got sick of it on their sixth trip, so I just locked the door. I know she has the key, but if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Then, on their seventh trip, the friend comes and can't open the door, so she starts banging on it like crazy. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back wherever she and my roommate were hanging out and got the key and came in. Then she told me it was very rude that I locked the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly said, "If you're going to make me get up and close the door, you can go through the process of unlocking it." My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. So, am I really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed? First, I need to consider the dynamics of shared living spaces. Dorm rooms are communal areas, and everyone has to share certain spaces and agree on how to use them. It seems like there's a conflict over the use of the door and the expectation of privacy. On one hand, I want privacy in my room, especially when my boyfriend is there. It's reasonable to expect that the door can be closed to ensure some level of privacy. On the other hand, my roommate and her friend seem to be using the open door as a way to express their annoyance or passive-aggressiveness. I also need to think about the actions I took. I locked the door after multiple instances of them leaving it open, which led to them being locked out. While I was trying to maintain my privacy, locking them out might have been seen as rude or aggressive, especially since they had the key. It's also important to consider communication. Did I address the issue with my roommate and her friend before taking the action of locking the door? It seems like I just kept closing the door each time they left it open, but I didn't have a conversation about why this was bothering me. Maybe if I had talked to them about how their actions were making me uncomfortable and asked them to close the door, it could have resolved the issue without needing to lock them out. Additionally, I need to reflect on the outcome. By locking the door, I was able to maintain my privacy, but it led to conflict and tension with my roommate and her friend. It might have been better to find a compromise or a different way to handle the situation that respects everyone's needs. In the end, while I understand wanting privacy, the way I handled the situation by locking them out might have been seen as overstepping or rude. It's possible that there's a better way to address the issue without causing conflict.
